newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends off on producer selling, imports.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends off on producer selling, imports.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed a see-saw session weaker, knocked from the highs by producer selling and soaring imports, market sources said.

Imports for the week ended Sept 8 totaled 42,913 bales and cumulative imports totaled 225,599 bales. The U.S. Department of Agriculture forecast imports at 500,000 bales in its monthly supply and demand report released Wednesday.
"Imports are the problem," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "If we maintain the current pace, we will be at or near the USDA estimate in a month."

Indeed, leading cotton merchant William B. Dunavant told a National Cotton Council (NCC) committee Wednesday that imports will continue to flood the U.S. market so long as domestic prices remain substantially higher than world prices.
December finished 0.11 lower at 75.96 cents a lb, having ranged from 76.47 to 75.25. Spot October ended 0.09 weaker at 74.81, while the back months closed 0.35 lower to 0.60 firmer.
Dealers called today's close bullish, and pegged support at 75.50 in December. "We have decent support underneath, and the specs are back to being long," a trader said.
Ganes said that while weak output will keep prices from sinking into the 60.00 to 70.00 cent a lb range in the near term, "recent lows are justified" based on the current supply and demand outlook.
The benchmark December contract reached a low of 72.60 September 10.
